reviews.body:
@pcbeingused333 thanks, the fix is correct: pandas `category` columns now fit as historical, future and static exogenous, and predictions match the same data with `object` columns exactly, including unused categories, a different category order, ordered and numeric categories, a `futr_df` with categories in another order, `cross_validation` and save/load. A few changes, see the inline comments.

This closes the pandas part of #1648. The polars `pl.Categorical` part is tracked in #1771, so nothing to change in the description for that.

review_comments.body: This calls the private `_encode_categoricals` on a `NeuralForecast` that was never fitted, with a hand-written mapping, so it doesn't go through `fit`, `predict` or `static_df`, where the error happened, and only the first case fails on `main`. Please add an end-to-end test parametrized over a historical, a future and a static categorical exogenous column: fit and predict once with `pd.Categorical` columns and once with the same data as `object`, and check the predictions are equal (they match exactly on this branch). Please include a `futr_df` whose categories are listed in a different order. With that in place, this unit test can go.
These lines are 92 and 105 characters. Please wrap the call and shorten the comment to stay under 88, e.g. `# map from object: a category dtype can't take the fill value 0`.
Please use the tuple form, `("values", "expected")`, and add `ids` (e.g. `["all_seen", "unseen"]`).

comments.body:
Replaced the private encoder unit test with a parametrized fit/predict comparison for historical, future and static exogenous columns, using explicit case IDs and reordered future categories. Wrapped the encoding call and shortened its comment as requested. All three cases reproduce the TypeError on main and pass with the fix on pandas 2.3.3.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
